samples.summary: The `replace` change to PrivateRoute/PublicRoute redirects has no test at all
samples.evidence: This delta's whole point in `PrivateRoute.tsx:36` and `PublicRoute.tsx:24` is that app-issued redirects must be `replace`, because `NavigationGuardProvider` guards pushes only (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-161: a push-form redirect would be refusable and, once Stayed, swallowed for good, stranding a signed-out user in a dialog / back-button loop). Nothing exercises either component: `grep -rn "PrivateRoute|PublicRoute" packages/frontend` returns only the source files, App.tsx and the README — no test file. The guard suite's closest test, `tests/components/navigation-guard/navigation-guard.test.tsx:166 'never refuses a redirect the app performs on its own behalf'`, uses a hand-written `<Link to="/login" replace>` in the harness, so it proves the provider lets a replace through but nothing ties that to PrivateRoute/PublicRoute actually issuing one. Dropping `replace` from either file (or any of the other `<Navigate ... replace>` sites the invariant now covers: file-detail.tsx:242,247, notes-detail.tsx:369, home-or-redirect.tsx:26, slides-detail.tsx:947, docs-detail.tsx:342, document-detail.tsx:863, board-detail.tsx:252) would ship green.

samples.summary: No test asserts the guard still works after a prompt is dropped by the location moving under it
samples.evidence: The new render-time drop block (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:191-195) clears `pendingRef`, `promptPathRef` and `prompt` together. The only test of that path, 'drops a prompt the app has already navigated past' (test:179-191), asserts only that the dialog is gone and the login page rendered. If a regression cleared `setPrompt` but left `pendingRef.current` set, the test still passes, yet every later guarded push would hit `if (!pendingRef.current)` as false and return without navigating and without a dialog — clicks silently doing nothing for the rest of the session. A follow-up assertion (navigate again under a blocking guard, expect the prompt to reappear) would close it.

samples.summary: The two new 'keeps the prompt' tests never answer the prompt they preserved, so the preserved pending navigation is unverified
samples.evidence: 'keeps a prompt a child effect raised in the commit that moved the location' (test:193-223) and 'keeps an open prompt through a query rewrite of the same page' (test:225-235) both stop at `expect(screen.getByText(PROMPT.title)).toBeInTheDocument()`. Neither clicks `PROMPT.confirmLabel`, so nothing checks that the surviving prompt's `pendingRef` still replays the right destination (/w/acme in the first case, /w/acme after the query rewrite in the second). A prompt kept alive but whose pending navigation was clobbered would pass both tests while the user's 'Leave' does nothing.

verdict.reason: No test in the repository exercises PrivateRoute or PublicRoute at all, so the `replace` semantics of their redirects are untested. A repo-wide grep for `PrivateRoute|PublicRoute` yields only the source files (PrivateRoute.tsx:11/36, PublicRoute.tsx:10/24), App.tsx:8-9,107,128, docs/README, and two test *comments* (navigation-guard.test.tsx:168, public-templates.test.tsx:88-92) — no test imports either component. The only test that mounts `<App />` (public-templates.test.tsx:6,88-101) renders `/templates`, a route deliberately outside PrivateRoute, and asserts the gallery renders; PrivateRoute's redirect branch is never mounted and PublicRoute never at all. The closest guard test (navigation-guard.test.tsx:58-62,166-177) uses a hand-written `<Link to="/login" replace>` harness, proving the provider allows a replace but not that either route component issues one. No indirect guard exists either: no ESLint rule or verify script mentions `Navigate` (scripts/ and eslint configs grep: no matches), and the repo's source-scanning invariant tests (preview-surface.test.tsx, detail-layout-subscriptions.test.ts, nav-items-single-source.test.ts, loader.test.tsx) check other properties; sibling sites such as file-detail.tsx:242,247 have a test file that asserts only back-button/Esc destinations (file-detail.test.tsx:138-210), never the redirect branches. Removing `replace` would ship green. In-lane (changed behavior with no meaningful test) and major, since the failure silently weakens a guard in a path signed-out users take.
